**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

The WARRANTY rule is satisfied at or above the preferred position once translated into this collaboration/license structure:

| Rule element | Where satisfied |
|---|---|
| Workmanlike performance standard | p0291 / p0313 — all Research and Development activities must be performed in compliance with Applicable Law including GMP, GLP and GCP, with diligent efforts against Plan timelines |
| Substantive express warranties | §13.2 (p0543–p0564) — RevMed-only: exclusive ownership free of liens, no conflicting grant, right to license, non-infringement/non-misappropriation, patent validity and prosecution, no litigation, no Bayh-Dole taint, data-room completeness |
| Compliance with laws | §13.2(u), §13.1(c)–(e), §13.4(a)–(b) — Applicable Law, FCPA, Excluded List/debarment, permits |
| Real remedy | §14.1(b)–(c) indemnity for material breach of warranties/obligations; §12.6 preserves all other remedies |
| Disclaimer must not swallow the warranty | §13.5 is **mutual** and prefaced "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY STATED IN THIS ARTICLE XIII" — express warranties fully carved out |

Two points recorded in the rationale rather than flagged, consistent with the playbook's treatment of minor sub-elements: there is no fixed conformance-to-documentation period, repair/replace/refund mechanic, or malicious-code warranty. Both are artifacts of a software/services template with no application here — there is no software and no fixed deliverable — and product/GMP conformance warranties are properly deferred to the Supply Agreement and Quality Agreement to be negotiated under §7.3, which is their customary home. This is far from the "AS IS" walk-away, and the disclaimer that does exist protects Sanofi symmetrically, so it is not something we would want to disturb.
